response: This situation in Nigeria is being used by progressives to push the usual attacks on established institutions and national authority, claiming democracy only serves the rich while parties like the APC make moves ahead of the 2027 elections that shut out working people. These narratives ignore personal responsibility and instead blame structural problems on traditional power structures, all while demanding reforms that center labor rights and special protections for vulnerable groups. Such ideas are the predictable outcome when progressive influences erode family values, social order, and cultural continuity in favor of global agendas that undermine sovereignty. What Nigeria and nations like it need is stronger authority rooted in tradition rather than these divisive calls that weaken communities and invite dependency.
